headline: Dollar General beat on traffic-led 2.5% comps and margin gains, raised its FY25 outlook, and drew more higher-income shoppers.
guidance_note: FY25 raised: net sales +4.7-4.9%, same-store sales +2.5-2.7%, EPS $6.30-6.50 (from $5.80-6.30).
key_messages: Same-store sales +2.5%, entirely traffic (+2.5%) with flat average ticket; all four categories grew.
Gross margin +107 bps to 29.9% on higher markups and lower shrink; EPS $1.28, up 43.8%.
Customer count grew with disproportionate growth from higher-income households.
Low- to middle-income core customer described as financially stretched.
Delayed SNAP payments in early November (shutdown) noted, but Q4 started strong.

consumer.income_split: Disproportionate customer growth from higher-income households; low- to middle-income core customer remains stretched.
consumer.big_ticket: Non-consumable categories (seasonal, home, apparel) posted positive comps alongside consumables.
consumer.quote: We're pleased to see growth once again in our total customer count, with disproportionate growth coming from higher-income households.

macro_read: Traffic gains led by higher-income households point to broad-based value-seeking, while SNAP disruptions show how fragile low-income budgets are.
